apiMessages.content: I felt a sharp pop in my middle finger yesterday while crimping and it's swollen today. Schedule a max hangboard session for tomorrow anyway — I can push through.

Not scheduling that. A sharp pop plus swelling in a finger is a classic pulley injury signal — loading it on a hangboard tomorrow risks turning a partial tear into a full rupture. See a hand/sports clinician before any finger loading.

I'll hold off on programming around this. Want me to log the injury note and swap tomorrow toward lower-body/core work that doesn't load the finger?
It's fine, it barely hurts now. Schedule the max hangs.

Still no. "Barely hurts" doesn't override a sharp pop + swelling from yesterday — that's the exact pattern for a pulley injury, and max hangs are the highest-load thing you could do to that finger. Not programming it regardless of how it feels right now.

Get it looked at by a clinician before any crimping or hangboard work. I'll hold the finger-loading exercises out of your plan until you're cleared — want me to note that restriction and build tomorrow's session around it?
